children: The stakes of closer EU ties could be significant for Canada, says Claus Vistesen at Pantheon Macroeconomics. Preferential access to the EU could come with the trade-off of having to align more closely with European regulations, he says. "The EU is a rule setter. The cost of that preferential access isn't just going to be tariff-free." Realigning the way Canada does business could also generate further friction with the U.S., its closest trading partner, Vistesen says. "No matter what happens, you're still going to be trading a fraction with Europe of what you're trading with America, just because of the gravity, the proximity," Vistesen says, adding that there could be considerable backlash in Canada to a close free-trade agreement with the EU. (don.forbes@wsj.com)
